headline: Chinese memory maker CXMT says it will launch server memory on a denser chip design by the end of 2026, a design that Samsung and SK hynix are also pursuing.
score_reason: Lowered from 7 to 5: we carried this same CXMT announcement on 11 Oct 2026 (item 34, score 6); today adds detail but no new event, and the launch date is the company's own target.
importance_line: If CXMT delivers, buyers of server memory could eventually get another maker alongside Samsung, SK hynix and Micron, but nothing has shipped, the date is CXMT's own target, and TrendForce says its first modules may use the new design only in part.
summary: Yicai Global reports, as relayed by TrendForce, that CXMT president Cao Kanyu told a chip conference on 10 Oct 2026 that the company plans to launch server memory modules on its 4F² design by year-end, a more compact memory-cell layout (four units of area per cell instead of six) said to fit 30 to 50 percent more memory into the same space. This follows our 11 Oct 2026 report from Wccftech; the new detail is that TrendForce, citing Economy Tribune, says Samsung has shown only a prototype and has no firm date for the design, and that a launch is not the same as high-volume production.
notes: Read on TrendForce (relays Yicai Global, MyDrivers, Economy Tribune, Money Today). The SCMP original (the pool item) returned 403, so the url is the TrendForce page where the text was read. Follow-up of the 11 Oct 2026 edition item 34 (Wccftech, score 6); the duplicate check should compare.
